newsitem.title: INDIA: India Corporation Bank plans rate cut to 14.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: India Corporation Bank plans rate cut to 14.5 pct.

text.p: State-run Corporation Bank is planning to cut its prime lending rate (PLR) to 14.5 percent per annum from 15.5 percent, a bank official said on Saturday.

The revised rates will come into effect after the bank's board of directors approves the change, he said. The bank proposes to keep a maximum spread of four percentage points above prime rate within which all loans will be classified.
The prime rate is what banks charge on loans to top rated companies. Other borrowers have to pay higher interest.

The bank's proposal to cut interest rates on its loans comes after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced a series of steps earlier on Saturday in its monetary policy for the second half 1996/97 (April-March) aimed at boosting liquidity and lowering interest rates.
The RBI announced cuts in banks' cash reserve ratios and lowered the cap on deposit interest rates in response to industry's complaints on the availability and cost of funds.
The RBI governor told reporters that he expected banks to cut their prime lending rates by at least one percentage point after the policy measures were unveiled.
Another large state-run bank, Bank of Baroda, has announced a cut in its prime lending rate by 50 basis points to 15 percent per annum.
